descripcion:
Loneliness feels like a personal failure. It isn't. It's an alarm - the same kind of equipment as hunger, thirst and pain, doing exactly what it was built to do.

Two hundred thousand years ago, being separated from your group didn't make you sad. It killed you. So your body evolved to make isolation hurt badly enough that you'd go and fix it. That alarm is still installed, still working, and still firing in a world it was never designed for.

In this video:

Sources: John Cacioppo, Loneliness: Human Nature and the Need for Social Connection (2008), on social pain, hypervigilance to social threat and fragmented sleep; Holt-Lunstad et al. 2010 meta-analysis on social connection and mortality; Dunbar on social network size; healed fractures in the fossil record as evidence of long-term care.
